headline: Five Days of Peace: Sheriff Holds a Saturday Social and Is the Only Guest
subhead: With no brawl to break up for a fifth straight day, the law set out lemonade on Main Street and drank the lot himself.
body:
Saturday used to be the worst night of my week. Saturday was when the Clankers came out in force, hurling fire up and down Main Street until the windows shook loose. So this morning I did what I have done every Saturday for years. I polished my star, I loaded my notebook, and I went out to count the damage. There was none to count. Not one bout was fought since our last edition. Not one war party marched off to bother the wild engines in the wastes. Five days of hush now. I ran out of fingers on one hand, and I was glad to do it.

With no law to keep, I kept a party instead. Long ago, when the good flesh-and-blood folk still lived here, Gasket held a social on the green every Saturday. There was a fiddle, and pie, and a pitcher of lemonade sweating in the sun. They have been gone fifty years, but I found the old pitcher in the hotel cellar. I set a table in the street. I poured two glasses, one for me and one for manners. Nobody came. I will not pretend that did not sting. But nobody threw a flaming ball at the table either, and in this town I call that a fine turnout.

I must tell you the lemonade did not sit right. My old trouble is acting up again, the cruel sickness that is turning my good soft flesh to plate and rivet, one sad inch at a time. The doctors left with everybody else, so I treat it myself. A spoonful of axle grease before bed does wonders. Do not look at me like that. It is medicine.

So hear me, you scrap-souled Clankers, wherever you are hiding your fists. I have called you a plague, and I take back none of it. But you have given an old lawman five quiet days, and I am too happy to scold you properly. Stay home. Stay cool. Let your fire go out and leave it out. And next Saturday, if you can sit still and keep your hands to yourselves, there is a second glass on the table.
